<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
# ⚠️ Warning: Availability gate failed

**Gate 1 (Availability ≥ 99.5%): FAILED.** Measured availability was **99.1%**, which is **0.4 percentage points below** the threshold. Over a 10,080-minute week, that is about **40 minutes** more downtime than the gate allows (≈ 90.7 min actual vs. ≈ 50.4 min permitted).

**Gate 2 (No incident > 60 min): Passed.** The longest incident was 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the limit.

---

# Weekly Availability Summary

| Metric | Value | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measured availability | 99.1% | ≥ 99.5% | ❌ Fail (−0.4 pp) |
| Incident count | 2 | — | — |
| Longest incident | 41 min | ≤ 60 min | ✅ Pass (19 min margin) |
| Shortest incident | 12 min | — | — |
| Total incident duration | 53 min | — | — |

**Overall: Did not meet targets** (1 of 2 gates failed).

### Note on a data discrepancy
The two recorded incidents total 53 minutes, which would correspond to about **99.47%** availability. The measured 99.1% implies about **90.7 minutes** of downtime, leaving roughly **38 minutes unaccounted for**. Possible causes include unlogged incidents, degraded-performance periods counted as unavailability, or a different measurement window or method. Either way, the gate still fails: even the 53 minutes alone would put availability just below 99.5%. I'd recommend reconciling the incident log against the availability measurement.
